newsitem.title: USA: Bronx leader runs for New York mayor.
newsitem.headline: Bronx leader runs for New York mayor.

text.p: Fernando Ferrer, a politician who has overseen the rebuilding of the Bronx from a national symbol of urban decay, Monday declared himself a candidate for the Democratic nomination for New York City mayor.

In a speech at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel in Manhattan where his grandmother worked for years in the kitchen, the Bronx Borough President sought to contrast his quieter style with that of tough-talking Republican incumbent Rudolph Giuliani.

"I am not a prosecutor, I am a planner," said Ferrer, who could become the city's first Hispanic mayor. "I am running not to attack, not to bully, not to threaten, but to rally, to lead, to inspire New York."

Former prosecutor Giuliani, known for his no-nonsense, brash approach to governing, narrowly won office from Democratic Mayor David Dinkins in the 1993 election and went on to see crime slashed to its lowest levels in a generation during his administration.

Ferrer joined black activist Rev. Al Sharpton and little-known Brooklyn councilman Sal Albanese in seeking the Democratic Party nomination. Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messinger is also expected to join the Democratic race.
Public opnion polls put Giuliani far ahead of all his potential rivals in the mayoral election in November. The Democratic primary is scheduled for September.

The 46-year-old Ferrer told hundreds of applauding supporters that since becoming Bronx Borough President in 1987, "nearly 30,000 affordable apartments stand in the place of burned out shells while the rest of the city was losing homes ... 10 years later thousands of families have lives of which they are now proud."
